# 1.2.94 - the messenger reads only what was seen, the Sound window saves as you go, the action and Call windows say what they can keep, and fixes for three faults the owner reported: the Projects window's two selects, the GM's room outline, the doorway light through a neighbour's walls

Stages E50 and E51 ship with this version, together. 1.2.94 is built on 1.2.93 (E90, the server-clock hotfix), which shipped
first (31.10.2026) and is included here; these notes do not repeat it. E50 is the messenger, which now counts a message as read only when
it was seen, and the Sound window, which now saves each change as it is made. E51 is small play and GM flows: the action
and Call windows, the map, the HUD, the trace, the trial, the panel and the handbooks. Three faults the owner reported on
31.10.2026 have fixes here, measured headless only: the Projects window showing both of its selects at once, the GM's room outline drawn
round a room the GM's token is not in, and a room frame's light showing through the next room's walls. (The Remnant and
project-token rings, gone in the same report, are 1.2.93's: E90 changed their cause, and their table check is LIVE-E90-01.) Nothing in this version has been run at a real table;
what was measured was measured on the headless harness. 29 commits on top of the 1.2.93 line (06556296), up to
2d8a11e4, the last before the release commit; 5 of them are merges. What was counted and what was not is in Known gaps
and Checked, and what only a table can settle is in Not checked at a real table yet.

## Before installing

1. **Back up the world, and note the version you ran,** so a problem can be traced back.
2. **What changes in a running world.**
   - **No migration is added** (`migrate.mjs` is not among the changed files) and `module.json` has no diff from 1.2.93 (it still reads 1.2.93; the release commit sets the version).
   - **One thing is removed from the world, once, at ready:** a Music mapping that names the "Situational" playlist. The
     primary GM's browser writes the whole map again without those keys, with no warning (a debug line only). The playlist
     itself stays the cue playlist of the Play tab; it only leaves the Music selects. Nothing else in the map is touched.
   - **A new GM store, `traceDigest`** (setting `gmTraceDigest`), holds the traces waiting for the time-of-day digest. It is
     shared by every GM, backed up, cut by the season reset's "remnants" group with the traces it names, and has no player
     copy. Until now that list sat in the memory of one GM's browser.
   - **A new client setting, `handbookBook`:** the handbook this browser last had open.
   - **Bridge and sockets.** No bridge action and no socket event is added. What changes on the bridge: a discard of a broken
     item is refused during the Class Trial ("that waits until the Class Trial is over"); after the primary GM places the
     trace of a player's discard it keeps a one-use ticket that the item's deletion then needs (see For the GM); an
     Objection or a re-point may aim only at the trial's participants; and the list of refusal texts gains "that action is
     denied by the incident".
   - **Texts and books.** `lang/en.json` +102 -15 lines and `lang/pl.json` +103 -18 against 1.2.93; the parity check read 4438
     English and 5289 Polish keys with none missing at 47b63d64. After 47b63d64 the two files changed in one Polish value
     only (`DRPG.Monocub.meddleRefused`), and a count of their leaf keys at HEAD reads the same 4438 and 5289; the parity
     check's own counts were not recorded again. The GM handbook and
     the player handbook, in English and Polish, changed (the sections are named below).
   - **Contract.** The register of places the module relies on (`patches.mjs`) gains one row, `token-ruler`, with its sentence
     in English and Polish (R1562) and a row in the GM handbooks' contract tables (EN and PL), "a token's ruler keeps Foundry's
     colour" (R1563).
3. **The owner's answers.**
   - **E50, 30.10.** Q-E50-2, -3 and -4 on their defaults ("Reszta pytan domyslnie"): a thread is seen when the messenger
     window is frontmost and the page visible; the primary waits 1500 ms after a mapping change before the music follows
     (plus 400 ms of its own settle); Foundry's curve is used for the Music slider only, the module's Sound slider stays
     linear. **Q-E50-1:** the owner asked what happens to the Situational playlist, was told, and chose to have a stored
     mapping onto it removed automatically (about 17:45Z), not kept and warned about. That is what the primary now does.
   - **E51, 30.10.** Q-E51 Q1 to Q8 all on their defaults ("Q-E51 wszystkie domyslnie"): "Trial grounds" means the Class
     Trial phase; a player with several characters and none assigned gets the controlled one, else the first by name, and a
     hint to assign one; the plan's "Project here: 3 actions left" item is dropped (E17 and E79 had already replaced that line); an Objection target who disconnected is still
     a target; the last handbook is kept in a client setting; the doubled character token goes to a table check (LIVE-E51-04);
     the doorway-glow fix lands only when the cause is found by reading (it was, after the owner's screenshot, below). **One default was
     changed by the fix round:** Q3 read "the trace digest syncs to the primary only". The end review measured that a trace a
     second GM places then reached no digest, and the store is now shared by every GM (FG1, below). The owner's answers file
     does not mention that change.
   - **E51, 31.10.** Added to the fix round by the owner: the Projects window shows only the select of the picked row; the
     GM's room outline sometimes on another room than the GM's token; the Remnant and project-token rings gone (1.2.93's, not
     this version's); the frame light through neighbouring walls. Answers to the fix round: (1) the Dynamic difficulty card
     still ends in "Answered by", and the result follows on a separate GM card - "Tak starczy", enough, no new bridge road;
     (2) a watched Sabotage that fails without Fear revealing it plays `sabotageFailed` for the saboteur, as before E51 - "Tak";
     (3) one sentence in the trust-model rules file on the discard ticket - "Tak".

## At the table

### For the GM

**The messenger (E50)**

- **A thread is read only when you can see it.** Each GM's browser keeps its own read marks: a thread counts as read while its
  window is in front, on its Chat tab, with the page visible. A message that comes while the window is behind another, on the
  Note tab or in a hidden browser tab raises its card and stays unread until you look. (The harness models "in front" and
  "page hidden"; v14 itself is LIVE-E50-01 and -02.)
- **Your own asks count.** An ask the module posts from your session (the bridge's cards in a player's thread) counts as
  unread for you until you read it or rule on it, and the launcher's badge is drawn again when such an ask settles. The
  threads are counted in one pass: for a launcher and a roster of 8 or more, the parent took 33 walks and 22 reads of the read
  map for 11 threads, and the tests now hold it to one walk and one read (R1065).
- **The roster closes by one road.** A click outside it, or on a row, closes it; pressing the launcher again does not open a
  second one.
- **A message deleted from the chat log leaves every open thread window.**

**The Sound window (E50)**

- **Every change saves as you make it.** The window has no Apply; a Music row says *Saving...*, then *Saved* (or *Not saved -
  see the console*), and every tab ends in one **Close**. Two GMs saving different rows in the same moment both keep theirs
  (measured on the harness with a stand-in for the second read, not with two real GMs).
- **The primary GM's music follows any GM's mapping,** about two seconds after the last change (the harness read 1904 ms for
  a second GM's change); several changes in a row are followed once. If the primary leaves inside that wait, the next primary
  applies the change.
- **One thing to know about two GMs.** A GM who takes a row out, or puts back the playlist it had, within about four seconds
  (4000 ms) of another GM changing that row, sees the other GM's choice come back once: the module cannot tell that write from
  two saves in the same moment. The next change stands. A write you make yourself, other than one the module sent, ends the
  watch at once.
- **A playlist that a state's mapping moves away from stops** when the primary follows the change (a mapped playlist that is
  also played by hand for another reason is stopped too; a state unmapped altogether still leaves its playlist playing).
- **The cue playlist ("Situational") is not offered** in the Music selects; see Before installing.
- **The times of day in the Sound window read in the table's language** (they read English on a Polish table before).
- **The Music slider is drawn on Foundry's own scale** for the playlist volume, so it should show the number Foundry's
  playlist slider shows: 50 writes 0.3536. Foundry's own functions are used where Foundry has them, else the same curve,
  read in a type package (fvtt-types 14.366), not in v14's code. The Sound slider stays a plain percentage.
  `game.drpg.setSfxVolume("music", v)` still takes a volume, as before, so a saved volume put back changes nothing.
- **The Sound window's failure texts and `diagnoseMusic` lines are localized** (English and Polish keys, `DRPG.Sound.why.*`,
  `DRPG.Music.diag.*`).
- **The murder music, read on four accounts.** On the harness the killer's, the victim's, the primary's and a second GM's
  browsers play the same track of 8, a bystander's none, and a slider moved during the incident holds after it. The harness
  plays no sound: this is the state each browser reads, not what was heard.

**Action and Call windows (E51)**

- **Thresholds are said before the roll and on the card.** The roll window shows the number to beat for the crisis roll (with
  the current Finishing Blow), the opening, and an item used from the sheet; Observe and Analyze identification are listed
  with the reason they show none. Result cards say "needed N" to the same recipients as before. A Palm roll's windows are
  titled by part and number ("Palm - Hand, beat 10"); the GM's tracker shows the last turns' total and threshold; a free
  crisis take is no longer printed as "0 >= N".
- **Observe tells you how the player looked** (general, non-obvious, follow traces) on the card in the player's thread, and
  its three hint texts no longer promise that the dice settle it (both languages).
- **Analyze's request box shows only with Hint,** and its stash and passage roads no longer forward a typed request.
- **The Projects window shows one select, the one for the picked row** (Work or Sabotage). The owner saw both at once.
  Read in the cascade for both themes (R1142, E51-T28); nobody has looked at it drawn.
- **A Role reversal the incident denied stays in the menu, struck through, with its reason,** and the GM still refuses the
  take.
- **A watched Sabotage makes one announcement and one sound** when Fear reveals it: one room card after the sabotage roll,
  the seen sound only when revealed. A watched failure without Fear plays `sabotageFailed`, as before E51.
- **A Dynamic miss gets a card** ("needed N"), also on a Reroll that misses again and on a turned success; the difficulty card
  itself still ends in "Answered by {name}" (the owner's answer 1 above).
- **Call windows come from one builder.** A Hope window is gold and a Despair window blood-red (read in the cascade, not
  looked at), the header is handed in, the GM road stays red, there is no "Do it". A window that stands stays live: Spend and
  the price line follow a Hope the GM grants while it is open, and a second press raises the window instead of opening a
  second one. Confusion names its thresholds in the choice window and on its card. The sheet's "call off the assembly" is now
  a Call window, **Call it off** (the default) or **Keep it**, not a Yes/No. The GM's approval window, Confusion and the
  call-off windows are not held to one at a time.
- **A refused Objection says what was refunded, or that the refund failed,** and a refund held back by a darkening is told
  once, not twice.

**The map (E51)**

- **The fog switched off is silent:** no layer, curtain, outline or sound; the discovery ledger still records.
- **A token placed in a room reveals it at once** and announces as a move would.
- **A doorway towards a room the veto keeps shut does not glow:** a locked room, a sealed one, another's Bedroom without its
  key. A Monokuma passes every door, as before. The standing outline is redrawn when a door, a wall, a room's flag, a seal or
  a chain changes, with no sound.
- **The GM's room outline follows the GM's own Monokuma token's room,** whichever token triggered the call (a GM with no
  Monokuma of their own, such as an Assistant GM with no pool, follows every Monokuma, as before). Four roads were measured on the harness, each
  red before and green after: a Monokuma move held for waypoints while another token steps (outlined mid Dorm A and after
  Dorm A, now Hall and Cafeteria); a trace placed during a held move (the trace's room, Gym, now Hall); a second Monokuma
  (placed in Storage, walked to Gym, now Hall); a region under the Monokuma edited (GO4). The fog itself still clears for every
  Monokuma on a GM's browser.
- **The room frame's light stops at the first wall and at the end of the room it falls into.** Read in the code before the
  fix: the light reached about 1.42 squares past its line on a straight border and 1.92 on a staircase, and walls were tested
  only out to 0.95 squares. Now the light is cut to a shape cast from each end of each segment, stopped by the first wall that
  stops a move (an open door does not) and where the ray leaves the room it entered. Measured on the harness with no renderer
  (R1138, R1139): with a wall at 1.0 or 1.3 squares the light ends there; with walls at 1.0, 1.3, 1.6 and 1.9 on a
  staircase each is stopped; a Hall one square deep with a Store behind it stops at 1.0. What the drawing looks like is
  LIVE-E51-03, whose text names the owner's screenshots of 11.10 and 31.10.
- **The token ruler takes the hour's colour** through a `token-ruler` row (the harness has no ruler class: R1115 reads the
  subclass on a stand-in; LIVE-E51-02).
- **A region's caption.** A region given Foundry's **Display Scrolling Text** shows its own text, since 1.2.94, and only over
  a token the browser shows. A token the room fog hides from a player, or every token in an Eclipse, gets no caption on that
  player's screen, unless a token that browser does show covers the same point (the check asks whether any shown token stands
  where the caption is drawn). Daggerheart's own captions over a token still never show. LIVE-E51-05.

**The HUD, the trace, the trial and the panel (E51)**

- **One viewer for a player with several characters** in the clock, the room tile and the explain window ("Where things stand"); the GM never
  gets the player's view in the status strip, and an Assistant GM with a student of their own gets the table's strip. The
  explain window's room section says to assign a character when there are several and none is assigned.
- **After a cast vote the Events card says the vote is in;** the overflow caption shows an armed or waiting darkening and
  its GM hint is true (a fourth tooltip, `gmHintQueued`).
- **The incident's turn card reaches the participants and the GM, not a bystander** (held by three defences on the harness).
  The Testimony card is held to a weaker promise: see Known gaps.
- **An undescribed trace is named by the neutral word,** *Trace*, in the reader's language, wherever a trace is named. A found trace
  from an incident reaches its finder like any other, and a described trace is marked edited. A new trace takes a spot
  in the same room and level when one is free (a spiral from its origin). **Clear Faint and Sweep show their result** in the
  dashboard window.
- **The trace digest survives the primary's F5 and any GM's traces reach it** (FG1). Any GM writes a row when a trace is
  placed; the primary alone says them at the turn of the time of day and drops each as it says it, so a new primary says
  what the last had not. Measured on the harness (scenario 61, TD1 to TD3): a second GM's trace, the primary leaving for good,
  a late primary. Read, not measured: a primary back from an F5 whose turn comes before its copy is complete may say a row
  again, one repeated card.
- **A debate opens at least 30 seconds on every road;** a shorter typed, remembered or handed-in length runs 30 and is
  remembered as 30. A debate again after an Overrule on 10 seconds left now opens 30, and its button reads "(30 s left)".
- **The trial console opens the evidence log.** The season form clamps the chapter, warns when saving moved the chapter during
  an Eclipse, opens a character's sheet by id (before, a row for Anna opened Ann's sheet), and fixes bad values quietly.
- **An Objection may aim only at the trial's participants,** in the picker and on the GM's side (a player's second character,
  a student a GM plays and a Monocub are not targets).
- **No discarding in the Class Trial:** the button is greyed with a reason, the player is refused, and the bridge refuses it.
  Outside the trial a discard now needs a one-use ticket: the primary GM writes it after it places the discard's trace (60 s,
  by character and item name cut to 80), the deletion that follows uses it, and a delete stamped as a discard with no ticket
  is flagged to the GMs like any bare delete (with Undo). This closed a way for a player's console to delete a module item
  with no roll, trace or card, in the trial too (scenario 30, D1 to D4). One road is still open: a player's console can ask
  for a discard's trace of its own choosing, with no roll behind it, and so earn the ticket for one deletion of that item
  name (measured by the verify review; named in the trust-model rules file).
- **The rules manager says what it did.** A write that failed is told as failed; an emptied rule keeps its old wording and
  you are told which; **Announce changes** is ticked by default and posts one card, *The killing game's rules have changed*,
  listing the rules introduced and those revoked (a rewording alone posts nothing).
- **The Players window counts characters,** not fields, in `applyAliveStates`; **every GM number field reads a whole
  number** (reads a typed 2.5 as 2). Small changes read through it: the round window's "0" seconds is the range's minimum, the
  Tier 0 item's effect is held to 0 to 12.
- **The handbook window keeps one language** after a declined reload and **opens on the book last read,** also after an F5.
  The checklist has a **First session** screen (the trial hall and its tokens, the school and hall linked, Foundry's
  settings, Dice So Nice); none of its rows is a step the GM panel's **Next** line waits on.

**Books and macros**

- GM handbook, English and Polish: 2 (First session), 6.2 (Announce changes), 6.3 (the messenger), 9.2 (region captions),
  15 (the 30 s debate floor, the console's evidence log), 17 (Sound), and the contract table's `token-ruler` row (20).
- `game.drpg.setSfxVolume` takes a volume, as in 1.2.93; `scripts/api.mjs` and `tools/api-surface.json` have no diff, so no name is added to or leaves `game.drpg`.

### For players

- **Read only when you look.** A message counts as read only while the thread's window is in front, on its Chat tab, with the
  browser tab you are looking at; otherwise its card shows and it stays unread. A message that fails to send stays in the
  box; one refused before it went (too long, no GM connected) says only why; one that did not go says "Your message was not
  sent. It is still in the box - try again.". During a killing your message is posted by the GM's browser, and when its answer
  does not come in time you see "Your message may not have been sent. It is still in the box - look at the thread before you
  send it again.": the GMs may have it all the same. A message a GM deletes leaves your open window too.
- **The Take on a body** says only what happened and opens again when nothing was taken (the GM's side refused it, no GM
  answered, or you play no character); one that took something stays pressed.
- **The Sound window for players** has the Music slider on Foundry's scale (see above).
- **Observe and Palm.** The Observe hints no longer say the dice settle it; in a room with nothing of the kind, the GM decides
  what you see. Palm's roll windows name the part and the number to beat.
- **Dead under an Eclipse:** a dead student is told they are dead, not that the Eclipse locks actions.
- **Role reversal** the incident denied is struck through, with its reason.
- **Reshape (Tamper)** now shows its trace select. Its show rule had no CSS line since E09, so the select was never shown and
  the first erasable trace was reshaped whatever the player meant. Both read in the cascade and the code (the correctness
  review; R1142), not looked at drawn.
- **No discarding during a Class Trial:** the button is greyed and its tooltip says *Nothing can be thrown away during the
  Class Trial.*
- **Objection** can be aimed only at a participant of the trial.
- **Call windows** are gold (Hope) or blood-red (Despair), stay current while open, and open once.
- **A player with several characters** gets the same one in the clock, the room tile and the explain window.
- **Project windows** show one select for the picked row.
- **A region's caption** shows over a token your browser shows (see For the GM).
- **Polish:** `DRPG.Monocub.meddleRefused` promised a refund the code does not give; it now says what English says.

### For everybody

- **No new packet and no new bridge action.** The new refusals are answers on roads that already exist (`remnant.place`,
  `trial.object`, `floor.repoint` and the crisis actions' guards), and the ticket is written on `remnant.place`.
- **The Polish and English texts of the new windows, cards and refusals are paired** (parity and prose checks green at the
  commits they ran on; figures in Before installing and Checked). Console lines stay English except the ones named above.
- **The handbooks changed** (EN and PL): player handbook sections on the messenger ("Read only when you look"), the Observe
  table, the Take, and no discard in the Class Trial.

## Known gaps

- **The Dynamic difficulty card** still ends in "Answered by {name}", by the owner's decision of 31.10; the roll and
  threshold follow on a second GM card.
- **E51-29, the Testimony card for a bystander.** The incident's turn card is held away from a bystander. The Testimony card
  is the trial's public state on every browser, so what is held is that a dead-and-undiscovered student with no part in the
  trial has no card marked their own and no turn window. Hiding the card itself would be a gate on `trialCard` that would tell
  that student something the others' screens do not; not built. Raised to the owner; no answer in the sources.
- **E51-49, scenario 88 is in the `ci` layer, not in the local gate.** Its layers are `ci` alone: it presses drawn windows, answers
  asked ones and forces rolls, which the sandbox adapter refuses. A local-gate version was asked of the owner; no answer.
- **A console can still earn a discard ticket** with a discard trace of its own choosing (above). The ticket is keyed by item
  name, so a second item of that name could be deleted on the first's ticket (read, not measured). A ticket is the primary's
  memory: an F5 or a handover between the trace and the delete costs one flagged card the GM can Keep (read, not measured).
- **Wall edits redraw the standing outline once per wall,** unbatched, on every browser, each a full redraw with the room's
  name shown again (read, not measured; `redrawFrameSoon`-style batching not built). **A token deleted, or a region changed,
  during a held move absorbs that move's arrival,** so its `roomEntered` sound and curtain are lost (read, not measured). A
  room reshaped while its outline stands keeps the old outline until the next arrival.
- **The doorway light** reads one-way and threshold walls as plain walls; R1138 runs at a canvas rect of {0, 0}, so a padded
  canvas is read, not measured.
- **A caption over a hidden token** still draws when a token this browser shows covers the same point (the GM handbooks say
  so).
- **Sound, small:** a state unmapped altogether still leaves its playlist playing; with the Sound window open on two GMs the
  other window's selects stay stale until it is opened again; `MAP_ECHO_MS` (4000 ms) is chosen, not measured.
- **Messenger, small:** on the "no answer in time" road the player sees two toasts (the bridge's "not carried out" and then
  "may not have been sent"); a GM refusal coded `failed` after a card was made, and "card made, words not kept", are read by
  no test.
- **Trace digest:** see the one repeated card above. **Spiral spots:** traces carry no floor of their own, so the room check
  of a new spot uses the source token's level.
- **Questions left on their defaults.** The Monocub gate in `performAction` moved above the death test with E51-06 (R86 holds that order), so a
  Monocub pressing a tile it may not dispatch in an Eclipse is told "only two actions"; asked of the owner, not answered. A
  living student is not put before a dead one by `chooseOwnStudent`; `overflowStatus().active` is unchanged for the
  Events panel's other readers; the First session rows never hold the Next line.
- **Wording not final.** The new Polish keys have had no read by a native speaker; the general text review (E65, E66, E71)
  takes them later. New windows' lines (`drpg-case-result`, the log button, the greyed Discard, the armed and waiting badges)
  have no CSS of their own and nobody has looked at them drawn.
- **Not measured at HEAD:** CI, `npm test` as a whole, the local gate, the whole of tier 2, the glass sweep as a whole, and
  scenarios 10, 13, 33, 50, 60, 62, 65, 67, 72, 83 and 00 at 7fa7302c or later (their last runs are at earlier commits of
  the range; 60 has no run in the sources).
